title: Mooring snap-back zones: why the whole mooring deck is a danger area
thumbnailText: THE WHOLE DECK IS THE ZONE

scenes.label: MOORING SAFETY
scenes.heading: You are outside the painted zone. Are you safe?
scenes.narration: You are standing outside the painted snap-back zone on the mooring deck. A line parts. Are you really safe?

scenes.label: TERM
scenes.heading: Snap-back zone
scenes.body: Where a parted line under load can recoil
scenes.narration: A snap-back zone is where a mooring line can whip back if it parts under load. The stored energy releases far too fast for anyone to step away.

scenes.label: WHY PAINT FAILS
scenes.heading: Paint can give a false sense of security
scenes.narration: The UK Code of Safe Working Practices advises against painting these zones. Leads around rollers and fairleads change the recoil path, so treat the whole mooring deck as a potential snap-back zone.

scenes.label: ON EVERY MOORING JOB
scenes.heading: Control the danger

items.title: Mark danger areas on the plan
Stay out of lines under load

scenes.narration: Assess the risk for the leads in use. Show hazard areas on the mooring plan. Hold a toolbox talk before every operation. And keep clear of any line under load.

scenes.label: KEY TAKEAWAY
scenes.heading: The whole deck is the danger zone
scenes.narration: Remember: on a mooring deck, there is no truly safe painted line.
